ES 2206 ( Part 3 ) ; 1989

Indian Standard

FLAMEPROOF ELECTRIC LIGHTING FITTINGS - SPECIFICATION
PART 3 FITTINGS USING FLUORESCENT LAMPS AND PLASTIC COVERS 1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 3 ) covers the range of fixed lighting fittings of flameproqf construction, intended for use where flammable gas or vapour may occur in explosive mixture with air. Flameproof fittings covered by this standard are those types using plastic tubes to enclose tubular fluorescent lamps ( Group I only ).
NOTE-The use of these fittings is restricted to Group I application only as certain of the gases and vapours in Group IIA and flB attack some plastics and cause a decrease in strength.

4 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Fittings shall comply with appropriate clauses of IS 2206 ( Part 1 ) : 1984 and requirement of IS 2148 : 1981 5 DESIGN, MATERIAL AND CONSTRUCTION 5.1 Lamps Fittings shall accommodate tubular fluorescent lamps of the appropriate wattage complying with IS 2418 ( Part 2 ) : 1977. 5.2 Lampholders Lampholders shall comply with IS 3323 : 1980 and be of such materials as to withstand the service temperature. 5.3 Control Gear and IntemaJ Wiring Discharge lamp auxiliary gear shall comply with IS 1534 ( Part 1 ) : 1977. All internal wiring shall comply with the appropriate Indian Standard and be such as to withstand the service temperatures. 5.4 Terminals Terminals shall comply with the requirements IS 2206 ( Part 1 ) : 1984. 5.5 Plastics Tubes The plastics tubes shall comply with the following requirements. 5.5.1 Composirion T&es made by a casting process, or by fabrication from thermoplastic sheet, shall be of unplasticized polymethyl-merhacrylate. Extruded tubes shall be made from unplasticized acrylic moulding powder. Tubes shall be free from the following defects: a) Crazing; b) Splits, cracks, air bubbles and foreign material; and C) Dirt specks .of area greater than 1'5 mm*. Acrylic moulding powder shall be free from dirt speck of area greater than 1'5 mm*, and from foreign material. 1 of

3 TERMINOLOGY 3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 2206 ( Part 1 ) : 1984 shaII apply.

IS2206(Part3):1989
5.5.2

Optical Properties Including Light Transmission

Tubes made from clear acrylic material shall have a light absorption not greater than 2 percent/cm of thickness. Optical characteristics of tubes shall be agreed to between the manufacturer of the material and the manufacturer of the fittings. 5.5.3 Finish of Surface Tubes made shall not be subjected to any surface finishing process which involves solvent etching. 5.5.4 Dimensions of Tubes The tub shall be circular in cross-section and the ratio of maximum to minimum diameter at any one cross-section shall not exceed 1'I. The wail thickness shall be not less than 6 percent of the nominal external diameter or 3'2 mm, whichever is the greater. 5.6 Mopptise of Plastics Tobes 5.6.1 The Plaoticetube shall be supported at both ends, the ends of the tube being mounted in or screw4 into ferrules which shall be affixed with an approved acrylic or epoxy cement ( see Fig. i and 2 ). The ieqh of the cement path shall be not less than one-third of the external diameter of the plastics tube, with a minimum of 25'4 mm. The plastics tube and cemented ferrules shall form a single replaceable unit.

NOTE - Cement joints are capable of withstanding compressive loads but have hmited ability to resist shear or tensile stremes; ferrules and associated supports should be designed with this in mind.

5.6.2 Air-tightness may be achieved by the use of ah appropriate type of gasket, which shall not be part of a flameproof path ( see Fig. 1 and 2 ). 5.7 Bodies of fittings and the ferrules shall be of metal. Provision shall be made, where desired, for the incorporation of the fluorescent lamp auxiliaries. The mounting of the lamp-holders shall be such as to take into account any permitted tolerances and any overall length for which the fitting is designed. Where the eietricai connections are housed within a coupling enclosure or tube, the end bodies, together with the said coupling, shall be designed and tested as an integral unit. 5.8 Fittings for Use with Cable Provision for the attachment of cable shall. be made in accordance with IS 2148 : 1981 and where necessary, IS 4821 : 1968 or other relevant Indian Standards. 5.9 Secnr@ Screws or Bolts Any external screws, hinges or bolts securing the various components of the fittings shall be of corrosion resistant metal, or be suitably treated to resist corrosion. Bolts, set screws, studs and nuts used to ensure the flameproofness of the enclosure shall comply with the requirement of 1S 2148 : 1981.

The reflectors shall comply with the relevant Indian Standards. 5.11 Provision for Guards Where required, pzovision shall be made for fixing efficient guards to protect against mechanical damage. 6 TEMPERATURE POSlTION RISE AND OPERATING

6.1 The maximum surface temperature rise shall not ejlceed 50�C ( range Z ), whatever the operating position, when measured in accordance with Annex D of Part 1 of this standard. 7 MARRING 7.1 Each fitting shall be permanently marked, either by raised lettering cast integrally with, or by a plate attached to the body of the fitting, in a manner which will not impair the flameproof enclosure, to indicate tbe following particulars: a) Name of the manufacturer, or his agent; ' b) Name ( or name and number ) by which the type is identified on the certificate;

8.1 Classification of Tests 8.1.1 Type Tests

8.2 Dimensional

Cheek-up

The lighting fittings shall be examined for the various dimensions and shall comply with the requirements of this specification. 8.3 Static Hydraulic Test Each tube, held at its seating surface only, shall be subjected to an internal hydraulic pressure of 10'50 kgf/cm', applied for a period of not less than 15 seconds, or more than 20 seconds. The pressure is to be brought up gradually to that value, the time taken being not more than 1 minute. For the purpose of this test the tube should be clamped between flat pressure plates with a suitable gasket material pressed against its ends. 8.4 Impact Text Tubes, when subjected to the test described in Annex C of Part 1 shall be capable of withstanding without perceptible damage an impact, normal to the contour of the tubes, of a 1'8 kg hammer falling from a height of 15'2 cm. 8.5 Temperature Rise Test
The maximum surface temperature rise shall not exceed 50�C ( range 2 ), whatever be the operating position, wben measured in accordance with Annex D of Part 1 of this standard.

The following shall constitute the type tests: a) Dimensional check up ( see 8.2 ), b) Static hydraulic test ( see 8.3 ), c) Impact test ( see 8.4 ), d) Test for temperature rise ( see 8.5 ), and e) Test for flameproofness ( Jee 8.6 ).
8.1.2 Acceptance Test

The following tests:

shall constitute

the acceptance

a) Dimensional check up ( see 8.2 ), b) Static hydraulic test ( see 8.3 ), c) Impact test ( see 8.4 ), and d) Test for temperature rise ( see 8.5 ). of samples for acceptance tests and criterion of approval shall be as glvcn in .Annex E of Part I of this standard. 8.1.3 Routine Tests The following shall constitute the routine tests: a) Dimensional check-up ( see 8.2 ), and b) Static hydraulic test ( see 8.3 ).
